title: Concurrency, throughput & the latency tradeoff
summary: When does increasing concurrency stop helping throughput and start hurting latency?

sections.title: The question
sections.text: More requests in flight can improve throughput. But when capacity is limited, waiting time can grow. I want to understand where that tradeoff appears and how to measure it clearly.

sections.title: The first experiment
sections.text: Start with a local Python simulation: 20 requests, each taking approximately 100 milliseconds, with concurrency limits of 1, 2, and 5. Predict the total duration before running the experiment, then compare it with measurements.

sections.title: What to measure
sections.text: Separate total run duration, per-request service time, and time spent waiting for a concurrency slot. Record the workload, configuration, errors, and sample size alongside the results.

sections.title: The limitation
sections.text: A fixed-delay simulation is a starting point, not a model-serving benchmark. Investigating saturation requires an explicit capacity constraint or a real bottleneck. Any later measurements will distinguish simulated workloads from real model inference.

sections.title: Current status
sections.text: This is an experiment brief. Implementation and measurements have not started, and no performance results are claimed.
